statement: Every normative, decision, version or integrity relevant field must be mechanically bound to its subject or checked against it. A field that is neither is removed rather than maintained: a statement that checks nothing and is checked by nothing is worse than none, because it feigns reliability. Purely descriptive metadata that carries no reliability claim is exempt, and the exemption is stated here so it is never later read as an omission.
method: For every candidate field, look for a place where its value is really compared to or checked against the subject it describes. Presence checks and plain reads do not count.

examined.subject: tools/guard/rules.json
examined.evidence: tools/guard/rules.py binds it to a signature over the loader's own field sets; a format change without a version change raises rules_format_signature_drift or rules_config_version_mismatch.
examined.reason: Named the configuration format and was compared to nothing. Binding carries over removal: applied to this repository's history it fails exactly at the commit where fixture_targets entered the format while the version stayed at 1.0.0, whereas removal would have detected nothing.

examined.subject: config/gates/blocks/*.json
examined.evidence: tools/gates/manifest.py compares it against ENGINE_VERSION; a manifest demanding a newer engine now fails with engine_too_old.
examined.reason: Claimed a minimum the engine had to meet and was only type checked, so a manifest could demand an engine newer than the one running it and the run proceeded anyway.

examined.subject: /usr/local/jarvis-guard/active.json
examined.evidence: The B0d check pl-source-commit rebuilds the package from the claimed commit object and compares it against the installed package_sha256.
examined.reason: Asserted the provenance of the installed package and nothing verified it. R6 checked declared expectations, not the installed manifest's own claim.

examined.subject: tools/guard/rules.json
examined.evidence: tools/guard/rules.py compares it against CONFIG_SCHEMA; tools/guardpkg/bootstrap.py compares the active manifest's copy against the package constant.

examined.subject: /usr/local/jarvis-guard/active.json
examined.evidence: tools/guardpkg/bootstrap.py rejects an unsupported value and compares it against the package constant.

examined.subject: /usr/local/jarvis-guard/active.json
examined.evidence: tools/guardpkg/bootstrap.py recomputes the digest of the installed files and compares.

examined.subject: /usr/local/jarvis-guard/active.json
examined.evidence: tools/guardpkg/bootstrap.py compares its real path against the root it was launched from.

examined.subject: /usr/local/jarvis-guard/active.json
examined.evidence: tools/guardpkg/bootstrap.py checks ownership over the whole ancestor chain of the declared and of the running interpreter.

examined.subject: exception object
examined.evidence: tools/guard/owner_exception.py version_bindings compares it; a mismatch classifies the object instead of releasing it.

examined.subject: config/gates/features/*.lineage.json
examined.evidence: tools/gates/features.py recomputes the predecessor digest and compares.

examined.subject: governance and gate configurations
examined.evidence: The responsible readers compare it, for example tools/decreg/model.py and tools/gates/errata.py; config/governance/config-loaders.json binds every configuration to such a reader.

examined.subject: /usr/local/jarvis-guard/active.json
examined.evidence: No decision, version or integrity conclusion is drawn from it anywhere.
examined.reason: A timestamp recording when the owner activated. It describes an event and asserts nothing that could be true or false about the installation, so there is no subject to bind it to. Deliberately kept and deliberately unbound.

examined.subject: config/gates/features/*.lineage.json
examined.evidence: The binding that carries the lineage is predecessor_feature_list_sha256, which is recomputed and compared.
examined.reason: An identifying label on the feature list. The integrity of the lineage rests on the digest, not on this name, so it makes no reliability claim of its own. Deliberately kept and deliberately unbound.
